ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Irène Joliot-Curie

code.originalText: Day 22 of cycle 1: bone marrow response, transfusion and infection review, and stopping venetoclax for count recovery

text.paragraph: Day 22 of cycle 1: bone marrow response and count recovery. [S]

Mrs. Joliot-Curie returns on day 22 of her first cycle. She spent five days in hospital for the ramp-up without tumor lysis. The nausea and constipation of the second week settled within three days on ondansetron and laxatives, and she has needed no ondansetron for a week. She has had no fever. She had one more unit of red cells and one dose of platelets on day 11 and none since. She had her bone marrow biopsy this morning. She has met the palliative care team again and the transplant center once. Her dose records have not yet arrived. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-19; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Tired but well; weight 52.8 kg; temperature 37.0 °C
Fine crackles at the right apex, unchanged
Two months of tiredness, easy bruising and bleeding gums, with pancytopenia and 12 percent blasts on the blood smear; acute leukemia suspected and urgent hematology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the bone marrow diagnosis two days later; its timing echoes the documented decline in her health (D).

Acute myeloid leukemia diagnosed on bone marrow biopsy (34 percent myeloblasts), in a physicist with decades of occupational exposure to ionizing radiation; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented leukemia
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis and subtype; the type of her real leukemia is not documented.

Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation over about four decades: X-ray work early in her career, laboratory work with polonium and other radioactive sources, and a laboratory accident in which a sealed polonium source ruptured on her bench about ten years ago
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented occupational exposure.
Pulmonary tuberculosis in her forties, treated to completion; no symptoms of active disease
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented tuberculosis; the treatment details are synthetic.

Moderately reduced lung gas transfer (DLCO 58 percent of predicted, FEV1 76 percent) from old tuberculous scarring of the right upper lobe; with performance status 2, it makes her unfit for intensive induction
S — Synthetic finding on pre-treatment testing.
Nausea with vomiting and constipation on day 11 of cycle 1 of azacitidine with venetoclax, without fever, with mild low potassium; managed as an outpatient; resolved
S — Synthetic treatment side effect; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Acute myeloid leukemia, day 22 of cycle 1 (C92.00). The day-22 marrow is hypocellular (about 10 percent) with 3 percent blasts: a leukemia-free marrow. Flow cytometry finds measurable residual disease at 0.6 percent. Neutrophils 0.2 and platelets 31 x10^3/uL: as planned when the marrow is clear, venetoclax is stopped today to let the counts recover, and the next cycle will begin when neutrophils are at least 0.5 and platelets at least 50, with venetoclax for 21 days. [S]
Stop venetoclax today; continue posaconazole, acyclovir and levofloxacin while neutropenic.
Stop allopurinol; tumor lysis risk has passed.
Blood count twice weekly; response review when counts recover.
Posaconazole trough level with the next blood count.

Nausea, vomiting and constipation, resolved (R11.2). Settled. [S]
Ondansetron and laxatives as needed only.

Missed: the posaconazole trough level due after about a week of dosing was not drawn. No harm judging by the absence of fever or fungal infection, normal liver tests, and a QTc of 446 ms on day 11. Corrective action: trough level with the next blood count, and added to the cycle order set
